newsitem.title: USA: New England Power Pool files for FERC restrcturing.
newsitem.headline: New England Power Pool files for FERC restrcturing.

text.p: New England Power Pool (NEPOOL) said Tuesday it has filed to restructure the New England wholesale electric power market as mandated under Federal Energy Regulatory Commission guidelines.

The proposal, based on FERC's ruling earlier this year, seeks to ensure non-discriminatory, open access to the regional transmission network that energy suppliers use to deliver energy to bulk users such as large industries, municipalities and utilities.
Among the proposal's key elements are a new tariff to be paid by NEPOOL members and the creation of an independent non-profit corporation in 1997 to oversee the new system.

NEPOOL said stakeholders with more than 90 percent of its voting shares support the proposal. NEPOOL has about 140 members, including Northeast Utilities, Boston Edison Co and New England Electric System.

NEPOOL spokesman William Sheperdson said the proposal "would allow any entity that pays the tariff to do business in the bulk power market" and theorhetically enable a utility outside New England to sell power to a New England community.
